_: ROADMAP K45(b3), re-banked by T-1127 for the field T-1123 enlarged. What the timber's detail control does. Read by tools/measure_timber_detail.mjs --gate, measured on the PUBLISHED mirror at 1280x800. The woody layer is planted over the whole field once rather than into a ring that follows the visitor, so unlike the sward its population does not depend on the viewport.
measured_against: the published mirror, walked through window.__chicago4d.setDetail

before._: the same three levels on the same mirror immediately before T-1127, when the keep fractions were 1.00 / 0.80 / 0.60 and every one of the three stem caps BOUND. The tree counts are the caps, exactly, which is what a bound cap looks like; max_station_n_m is the reading that says it truncated rather than thinned, against a field that runs to N +1117.8 m. `uncapped` is the same tree with the caps lifted so the loop could finish — the wood the records actually ask for, one wood counted at three sampling steps.

uncapped._: at the OLD 1.00 / 0.80 / 0.60 fractions, so the step-neutral demand is 4052 / 3981 / 3970 — the same wood at three grids. The 2026-08-17 banking of this file measured full at 472 trees, before T-1123 carried the ground north into Kinzie's Addition.

k45b3._: the three levels before K45(b3) gave the timber a thinning instrument at all, on the pre-T-1123 field. Kept because it is the measurement that says the caps were once inert: 472/470/437 is one wood planted three times.

tolerance._: tree_share is checked against the level's keep DIVIDED BY full's keep, not against the keep itself: since T-1127 full's keep is 0.400 rather than 1.00, so 'the fraction of the roll' and 'the fraction of full's trees' are different numbers and only the second is a ratio between levels. A Bernoulli acceptance over ~190,000 cells is near-Poisson, and the count carries a second error the sampling step contributes on its own — before any keep fraction existed the three levels planted 472/470/437, so light's grid alone reads 7 % below full's. Measured today the two lower levels sit 4.6 and 1.6 points off their nominal shares of 87.5 % and 56.3 %. band_share is the northernmost tenth of the swept field's share of the STEMS, and a truncated wood empties it outright (before T-1127, full's top band held 39 % of its stems and light's 12.7 %). It was 0.04 and is 0.05, because the denominator counts the point-bar screen, which deliberately does NOT thin: at a lower level the unthinned stools are a larger share of a smaller stem count, and they stand on the river rather than in the north. Measured today the spread is 0.044 across three levels that all reach the same latitude — composition, not truncation, and 0.05 still catches an emptied band by an order of magnitude.

reach._: The swept field runs to N +1117.8 m since T-1123 carried the ground north into Kinzie's Addition. A stem budget bound partway through a south-to-north loop pulls this down: that is what K45(b2) found at light's old cap of 300 and what T-1127 found again at all three caps, which stopped the wood at N +949.8 / +803.3 / +722.6 m. The floor was 385 m, sized for the pre-T-1123 field; it is now 1100 m, which no truncation of any consequence can clear.

screen._: The sandbar-willow point bar. It does not take the keep fraction — a screen needs its clumps to touch — and since K45(b3) it does not thin with the sampling step either. The floor is under 1 because a 6-9 m bar sampled on a 5.6 m grid has fewer points than the screen wants stools, and the roll saturates at 1 rather than exceeding it. It was 0.65 on the pre-T-1123 field and is 0.60 now: the enlarged field carries more bank, so the residual a coarse grid cannot resolve is larger in absolute terms. Measured today light keeps 64.3 % of full's stools, against 51.6 % before K45(b3) existed.
